`dispatch_forwards_model_and_runs_in_per_ticket_worktree` (asserts `request.cwd == worktree_root/<id>`, not the shared root), `missing_adapter_does_not_strand_ticket_inflight`, `host_failure_releases_ticket_and_returns_err`. Existing tests updated to init a real git repo via `tempfile`.

- `cargo fmt --all`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: `Finished` — 0 warnings
- `cargo test --workspace`: all suites `ok`, 0 failed (new tests confirmed passing by name: `missing_adapter_does_not_strand_ticket_inflight`, `host_failure_releases_ticket_and_returns_err`, `dispatch_forwards_model_and_runs_in_per_ticket_worktree`, `migration_0003_preserves_hand_references_from_v2`).

input.title: Add success-path worktree cleanup for local hand dispatchers
input.prompt:
Both local hand dispatchers create per-ticket git worktrees via raw `git worktree add` and never clean them up on a SUCCESSFUL dispatch, so `.derrick/copilot-worktrees/<ticket-id>` and `.derrick/host-worktrees/<ticket-id>` checkouts accumulate over time. They are NOT tracked by the substrate `reserve_worktree` row, so the foreman TTL pruning pass (`list_stale_open_worktrees` in crates/derrick-substrate-native/src/foreman.rs ~635) never removes them. Only the failure path removes the worktree.

Affected:
- crates/derrick-copilot/src/local_dispatcher.rs (LocalCopilotHandDispatcher) — pre-existing.
- crates/derrick-hand/src/lib.rs (HostCliHandDispatcher, added in D66) — matches the same pattern deliberately.

Goal: give per-ticket hand worktrees a real lifecycle. Options to evaluate: (a) register them as substrate worktree rows (reserve_worktree/close_worktree, but those are keyed on run_id today — may need a ticket-keyed variant) so the foreman TTL pass prunes abandoned ones; or (b) remove the worktree once the ticket reaches a terminal state (InReview/Done/merged) via the foreman reconcile path — but confirm the verify/merge flow doesn't still need the checkout before removing it. Fix BOTH dispatchers together so they stay behaviourally identical. Add tests for the chosen cleanup trigger.

Context: introduced/observed during D66 (host-executor model forwarding + host-CLI crew hands), PR for branch feat/host-executor-model-forwarding. A Codex review flagged it MAJOR; we judged it a pre-existing cross-cutting gap and deferred it rather than gold-plate only the new dispatcher.
input.tldr: Per-ticket hand worktrees are never cleaned up after a successful dispatch (untracked by the foreman's TTL pruning), so they accumulate. Affects both the local Copilot hand and the new host-CLI hand — fix the lifecycle for both together.

> **Stacked on #19** (base = `feat/host-cli-only-models-d64`). Review/merge #19 first; this retargets to `main` once #19 lands.

## What & why

Follow-up to D65. Two gaps surfaced: (1) the model you configure in `derrick.yaml` was **never forwarded** to the host CLI on the run path — every host (copilot included) used its own default; (2) opencode/codex/aider were first-class *pipeline hosts* but **couldn't be crew executors** (`hand_kind_for_executor` mapped everything but copilot/claude to a `Human` hand). This PR makes the configured model drive `--model`, and makes opencode/codex/aider real crew executor hands. Recorded as **D66** (refines D65/§6.5).

## Part A — pipeline `host:` steps forward the model
`execute_role_step` resolves the step's role → `ModelDef.model()` and sets `HostRequest.model` (raw id; the adapter normalises per D65). Empty/whitespace → `None` (host keeps its default). All five hosts now honour the configured model on the run path.

## Part B — opencode/codex/aider as crew executor hands
- **New `HandKind` variants** `Codex`/`Opencode`/`Aider` (enum + `Display`/`FromStr`, snake_case in lockstep).
- **Migration `0003`** rebuilds the `hands` table to widen the `kind` CHECK, preserving the `tickets.owner` / `events.scope_hand` FKs (FK-off rebuild + `foreign_key_check` guard, `user_version=3`). Includes a **v2→v3 regression test** asserting hand-owned rows/FKs survive.
- **New crate `derrick-hand`**: `HostCliHandDispatcher` executes an assigned ticket through the **derrick-tools host adapter** (so D65 `--model` normalisation + headless flags apply) in a **per-ticket git worktree** (mirrors `LocalCopilotHandDispatcher`, so concurrent hands never share an index). Adapter + worktree are resolved **before** `assign_to_hand`; any post-assign failure releases the ticket, removes the worktree, and returns `Err` (so the foreman never records a failed dispatch as dispatched).
- **Foreman wiring**: `build_dispatcher` resolves the executor model and registers a `HostCliHandDispatcher` (shared `Arc<HostRegistry>`) for codex/opencode/aider. **Copilot stays the GitHub-cloud hand** (model is server-side — no `--model`). Claude/Copilot dispatchers untouched.

## Reviewer notes
- **Known limitation (tracked follow-up):** a *successful* dispatch leaves the per-ticket worktree on disk — this exactly matches the existing `LocalCopilotHandDispatcher`, and neither is pruned by the foreman TTL pass (they aren't substrate-tracked `reserve_worktree` rows). Deferred deliberately rather than gold-plate only the new dispatcher; a follow-up will give both a real cleanup lifecycle.
- **Deferred:** per-host `tools.{codex,opencode,aider}` config blocks (MVP uses sensible poll defaults); folding the Claude dispatcher onto the generic host-CLI path.
- Validated with **two Codex read-only review passes**; all blocking/major findings addressed. `cargo fmt` + `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` + `cargo test --workspace` green (52 ok blocks, 0 failures).

## Summary: Existing Size/Complexity Signals for Foreman Adaptive Model Selection

Based on thorough investigation of the derrick workspace, here is the concrete answer to whether existing per-ticket signals exist for adaptive model selection:

### What EXISTS (signals available at dispatch time):

1. **Ticket body text length** (cheap to compute): The `Ticket` struct contains a `body: String` field (types.rs:615-643). At dispatch time in the foreman loop (steps.rs:649), you have the full ticket including its body. You could count lines, character count, or estimate tokens from the markdown task that was parsed.

2. **Ticket ordinal** (trivial): Every ticket has an `ordinal: Option<u32>` field (types.rs:620). Small ordinal → early in the batch, potentially simpler bootstrap tasks. Large ordinal → later, potentially complex work.

3. **Batch size** (available): The batch itself is known at dispatch time. You could count how many ready tickets exist in the same batch—batch-level parallelism signals whether work is fine-grained or large-scale.

4. **Executor model metadata**: At dispatch (steps.rs:598), you already select a model and call `hand_kind_for_executor(provider, cli)`. Cost hints exist in derrick_models (lib.rs:157, builtin_cost_hint), so you can look up model capabilities (input/output pricing, latency tier) and make selection decisions *before* dispatching based on ticket properties.

### What DOES NOT EXIST (no built-in signals):

- **No explicit `size`, `complexity`, `effort`, or `estimate` fields** on `Ticket` or `Batch` structs
- **No assay complexity scoring**: The assay (derrick-assay/src/types.rs) produces `ReviewerOutcome` with verdicts ("accept"/"revise"/"reject") and token counts, but no complexity or risk score attached to tickets
- **No task-level metadata** from speckit: When tasks.md is parsed (steps.rs:705-760), the bridge step extracts only `title`, `body`, and hardcodes a `["task"]` label. Any size/complexity hints from the original speckit task (if they existed in the spec) are dropped—only the text is preserved
- **No dependency graph** or file-set metadata on tickets—just title, body, ordinal, batch

### Current Dispatch Logic (steps.rs:649-679):

```rust
for ticket in &ready {
    let ordinal = ticket.ordinal.unwrap_or(0);
    match substrate.assign_to_hand(&ticket.id, &hand_id).await {
        // Dispatch all ready tickets to the same hand (executor/model pair).
        // No filtering, no per-ticket model selection.
    }
}
```

The foreman **does not currently pick a model per ticket**—it assigns all ready tickets to one hand based on the executor role. Model selection happens at the *step* level (which role/model is assigned to the foreman step), not per-ticket.

### Recommendation:

To implement adaptive model selection per ticket, you have two paths:

1. **Heuristic (cheap, no new fields)**:
   - Measure `ticket.body.lines().count()` or `ticket.body.len()`
   - Use `ticket.ordinal` as a sequencing signal
   - Optionally count batch size (`ready.len()`)
   - Map (body_size, ordinal) → HandKind/model choice at dispatch time
   - **Pro**: No schema changes, zero latency. **Con**: Heuristic may not capture true complexity.

2. **Structured (requires new schema)**:
   - Add a `complexity: Option<Complexity>` or `estimated_tokens: Option<u32>` field to `NewTicket` and `Ticket`
   - Have the bridge step estimate it when parsing tasks (e.g., line count × 4 tokens/line rule-of-thumb, or query the assay beforehand)
   - Let foreman dispatch use that field to select the model
   - **Pro**: Explicit, maintainable, can encode domain knowledge. **Con**: Requires schema migration, bridge step changes.

The heuristic approach is fastest to prototype; the structured approach is cleaner if complexity estimation becomes important elsewhere in the system.

SQLite `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` with a `NULL`-able column and no new CHECK that touches existing rows is fully supported and cheap. You do **not** need the `tickets_new` rebuild that `0002` used (that was only because you were tightening the `state` CHECK). Migration `0004` can be a one-liner `ALTER TABLE tickets ADD COLUMN complexity TEXT NULL`. If you want a CHECK on the enum values, add `CHECK (complexity IS NULL OR complexity IN ('low','standard','heavy'))` — `ADD COLUMN` *does* support a column-level CHECK, and since all existing rows get `NULL` it passes. This avoids the FK-off rebuild ceremony in `run_migration_0002/0003`.

**C. The `tasks` step is a host/LLM step (steps.rs ~927 routing → the host-step executor at ~206), producing `tasks.md` via the speckit `/tasks` template.** The bridge (`parse_tasks_from_markdown`, steps.rs:705) parses it. So the producer mechanism is: annotate the `/tasks` prompt to emit a marker, parse it in the bridge. The assay is a *reviewer/verdict* step, not a per-task producer — it is the wrong tool for this. Recommendation below confirms the tasks-step+bridge approach but hardens the parse.

## Point 2 — Producer (tasks step + bridge parse)

**Mechanism (recommended, robust):** annotate the `/tasks` generation prompt to emit, on the heading line of each task, a trailing tag:
```
## Wire up the migration runner  <!-- complexity: heavy -->
```
or a bracket form `## [H] Wire up...`. **Prefer the HTML-comment form** — it survives markdown rendering, never collides with a real title, and is trivially strippable. Parse in `parse_tasks_from_markdown` (steps.rs:723) where `## ` titles are detected:

```rust
if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_prefix("## ") {
    let (title, complexity) = parse_complexity_marker(rest); // splits off <!-- complexity: X -->
    // store title; carry `complexity` into the NewTicket built at the next heading / EOF

The tasks-step is the natural producer because the bridge already converts its output 1:1 into tickets.

**Fragility risk (flagged):** prompt-emitted markers are best-effort. Mitigation: (1) `None`→Standard fallback means a missing tag is harmless; (2) add one parse unit test per marker shape; (3) keep the marker regex permissive (case-insensitive `low|standard|heavy|l|s|h`). pub fn model_for_tier(&self, host: &str, tier: Tier) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let entry = self.host(host)?;
    if entry.tiers.is_empty() { return entry.default_model; } // hosts w/o tier metadata

        .or_else(|| entry.tiers.last().map(|(_,m)| *m))
}

## Point 4 — `auto` sentinel end-to-end

Introduce a `ModelChoice` derived from the RAW model string, parsed at the **edge** (where `def.model()` is read), so the config layer stays a dumb string store and validation stays tolerant.

```rust
// New: crates/derrick-tools/src/catalogue.rs (or a small new module reachable by hand + cli)
pub enum ModelChoice {
    Pinned(String),                 // concrete id -> always wins
    Auto { bias: Option<Tier> },    // "auto" | "auto:light" | "auto:heavy"
}
pub fn parse_model_choice(raw: &str) -> ModelChoice {
    match raw.trim() {
        "auto" => ModelChoice::Auto { bias: None },
        "auto:light" => ModelChoice::Auto { bias: Some(Tier::Light) },
        "auto:heavy" => ModelChoice::Auto { bias: Some(Tier::Heavy) },
        "auto:standard" => ModelChoice::Auto { bias: Some(Tier::Standard) },
        other => ModelChoice::Pinned(other.to_owned()),
    }
}
```

pub struct HostCliHandDispatcher {
    // ...
    model_choice: ModelChoice,   // was: model: Option<String>
    // ...

fn select_model(&self, ticket: &Ticket) -> Option<String> {
    match &self.model_choice {
        ModelChoice::Pinned(id) => Some(id.clone()),  // PINNED always wins
        ModelChoice::Auto { bias } => {
            let tier = bias.unwrap_or_else(|| match ticket.complexity {
                Some(Complexity::Low) => Tier::Light,
                Some(Complexity::Heavy) => Tier::Heavy,
                Some(Complexity::Standard) | None => Tier::Standard, // None -> Standard default

                .model_for_tier(self.host_name, tier)
                .map(|m| m.to_owned())            // None for copilot (unreachable here) -> CLI default
        }
    }
}

# Refined Design: Foreman-Driven Adaptive Model Selection

## Verification corrections to the brief (read these first)

Three things in the brief need adjusting before the plan is sound:

**A. There are TWO foreman code paths, and only ONE is the load-bearing one.**
- `crates/derrick-flow/src/steps.rs:568` `execute_foreman` is the *pipeline* foreman step. It does **not** construct a `HostCliHandDispatcher` and does **not** pass a model to any CLI — it just loops `assign_to_hand` (line 651). Model selection is irrelevant here; it never dispatches to a host CLI. **No change needed here** beyond optionally surfacing complexity in the log line.
- `crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/foreman.rs` `build_dispatcher` (the daemon, line ~162-187) is where `HostCliHandDispatcher::new(..., model, ...)` is constructed with a single fixed model. **This is the only place the per-ticket model restructure matters.**

The brief conflates these. The restructure (point 5) lives entirely in `derrick-hand` + `foreman.rs build_dispatcher`. The `execute_foreman` pipeline step is out of scope.

**B. `ADD COLUMN` on `tickets` is clean — NO rebuild dance required.** The `tickets` table CHECK constraints (`0002`, schema in lib.rs migration) are on `state`, `block_reason`, and `(ordinal/batch)` — none reference a new `complexity` column. SQLite `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` with a `NULL`-able column and no new CHECK that touches existing rows is fully supported and cheap. You do **not** need the `tickets_new` rebuild that `0002` used (that was only because you were tightening the `state` CHECK). Migration `0004` can be a one-liner `ALTER TABLE tickets ADD COLUMN complexity TEXT NULL`. If you want a CHECK on the enum values, add `CHECK (complexity IS NULL OR complexity IN ('low','standard','heavy'))` — `ADD COLUMN` *does* support a column-level CHECK, and since all existing rows get `NULL` it passes. This avoids the FK-off rebuild ceremony in `run_migration_0002/0003`.

**C. The `tasks` step is a host/LLM step (steps.rs ~927 routing → the host-step executor at ~206), producing `tasks.md` via the speckit `/tasks` template.** The bridge (`parse_tasks_from_markdown`, steps.rs:705) parses it. So the producer mechanism is: annotate the `/tasks` prompt to emit a marker, parse it in the bridge. The assay is a *reviewer/verdict* step, not a per-task producer — it is the wrong tool for this. Recommendation below confirms the tasks-step+bridge approach but hardens the parse.

---

## Point 1 — Ticket complexity field

**Enum shape:** `Low | Standard | Heavy` (maps to the catalogue tiers light/standard/heavy 1:1, avoids a second vocabulary). Put it in `derrick-substrate`:

```rust
// crates/derrick-substrate/src/types.rs (near Ticket, ~615)
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum Complexity { Low, Standard, Heavy }

impl Complexity {
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str { match self { Self::Low=>"low", Self::Standard=>"standard", Self::Heavy=>"heavy" } }
}
impl FromStr for Complexity { /* low|standard|heavy -> Ok, else SubstrateError::invalid */ }
impl fmt::Display for Complexity { /* as_str */ }
```

**Ticket field:** add `pub complexity: Option<Complexity>` to `Ticket` (types.rs:617) and `pub complexity: Option<Complexity>` to `NewTicket` (types.rs:706). `None` = "unspecified". **Default-at-selection is `Standard`** (resolved in `select_model`, never written to the DB — keeps "unspecified" distinguishable from "explicitly standard").

`NewTicket::new` (types.rs:723) gains a `complexity: Option<Complexity>` parameter. This is a **breaking signature change** — every caller updates (see blast radius). Alternatively add a builder `with_complexity` and keep `new` as-is defaulting to `None` — **recommended**, since `NewTicket::new` has ~5+ call sites including tests (derrick-hand tests line 524, the bridge twice). Keep `new` taking `None` implicitly is not possible without changing the signature, so: **add `NewTicket::new` a new arg OR add a `complexity` public field set after construction.** Cleanest: make `complexity` a public field, default it in `new` to `None`, and let the bridge set `ticket.complexity = ...` after `NewTicket::new(...)`. That touches zero existing `new` callers.

**Migration 0004** (`crates/derrick-substrate-native/migrations/0004_ticket_complexity.sql`):
```sql
ALTER TABLE tickets ADD COLUMN complexity TEXT NULL
  CHECK (complexity IS NULL OR complexity IN ('low','standard','heavy'));
PRAGMA user_version = 4;
```
Runner: bump `SCHEMA_VERSION = 4` (lib.rs:19), add `MIGRATION_0004` const, add a `run_migration_0004` that runs the batch in a transaction (no FK-off needed — no table drop). In `migrate()` (lib.rs:1975) add:
```rust
let version = ... ; if version < 4 { run_migration_0004(connection)?; }
```
`run_migration_0004` can be a *plain* transactioned `execute_batch` (model it on the inner closure of `run_migration_0002` but **drop** the `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` and the `foreign_key_check` — they are unnecessary for a pure ADD COLUMN).

**INSERT path** (lib.rs:637): add `complexity` to the column list and bind `ticket.complexity.map(|c| c.as_str())`. **Decode** (`ticket_base_from_row`, lib.rs:2467): the SELECT lists are at lib.rs:2296 (`select_optional_ticket`) — add `complexity` to the column list and read `row.get(11)` → `parse_optional_in_row(.., Complexity::from_str)`. Note: column indices shift; `complexity` goes after `updated_at` so existing `row.get(9/10)` are unaffected; new column is index 11. **Check every SELECT that feeds `ticket_base_from_row`** — grep shows only `select_optional_ticket` uses that decoder; `select_ticket_ids` (line 2253) only selects `id`, so it is fine.

---

## Point 2 — Producer (tasks step + bridge parse)

**Mechanism (recommended, robust):** annotate the `/tasks` generation prompt to emit, on the heading line of each task, a trailing tag:
```
## Wire up the migration runner  <!-- complexity: heavy -->
```
or a bracket form `## [H] Wire up...`. **Prefer the HTML-comment form** — it survives markdown rendering, never collides with a real title, and is trivially strippable. Parse in `parse_tasks_from_markdown` (steps.rs:723) where `## ` titles are detected:

```rust
if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_prefix("## ") {
    let (title, complexity) = parse_complexity_marker(rest); // splits off <!-- complexity: X -->
    // store title; carry `complexity` into the NewTicket built at the next heading / EOF
}
```
Set `nt.complexity = complexity` on the `NewTicket` before pushing (two push sites: steps.rs:728 and 756). `parse_complexity_marker` returns `(clean_title, Option<Complexity>)`; unknown/malformed marker → `None` (never error — the title is more important than the tag).

**Fallback when the model omits it:** `None` → resolves to `Standard` at selection. This is the safe default and requires no special handling. Do **not** fail the bridge on a missing marker.

**Why not the assay:** the assay is a downstream reviewer producing `assay/verdict.md` (steps.rs:934), running *after* tickets exist. It does not produce per-task rows and would require a write-back path into already-created tickets. The tasks-step is the natural producer because the bridge already converts its output 1:1 into tickets.

**Fragility risk (flagged):** prompt-emitted markers are best-effort. Mitigation: (1) `None`→Standard fallback means a missing tag is harmless; (2) add one parse unit test per marker shape; (3) keep the marker regex permissive (case-insensitive `low|standard|heavy|l|s|h`). Accept that complexity is advisory, not guaranteed.

---

## Point 3 — Catalogue tiers

Extend `HostModels` (catalogue.rs:26) with an **ordered tier table**, not three `Option` fields (an ordered slice lets `model_for_tier` fall back gracefully and keeps the `const` ergonomic):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum Tier { Light, Standard, Heavy }

pub struct HostModels {
    pub host: &'static str,
    pub default_model: Option<&'static str>,
    pub known: &'static [&'static str],
    pub id_style: ModelIdStyle,
    pub tiers: &'static [(Tier, &'static str)], // NEW; ordered light->heavy, may be empty
}
```

`model_for_tier` on `HostCatalogue`:
```rust
pub fn model_for_tier(&self, host: &str, tier: Tier) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let entry = self.host(host)?;
    if entry.tiers.is_empty() { return entry.default_model; } // hosts w/o tier metadata
    entry.tiers.iter().find(|(t,_)| *t == tier).map(|(_,m)| *m)
        .or(entry.default_model)
        .or_else(|| entry.tiers.last().map(|(_,m)| *m))
}
```

Populate (May-2026 ids from the existing table):
- claude: `[(Light,"claude-haiku-4-5"),(Standard,"claude-sonnet-4-6"),(Heavy,"claude-opus-4-8")]`
- codex: `[(Light,"gpt-5.4-mini"),(Standard,"gpt-5.4"),(Heavy,"gpt-5.5")]` (gpt-5.2-codex stays in `known` but off-tier)
- copilot: `&[]` (tiers irrelevant — cloud, no `--model`; see point 4)
- opencode: `[(Light,"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"),(Standard,"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"),(Heavy,"anthropic/claude-opus-4-8")]`
- aider: `[(Standard,"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"),(Heavy,"openai/gpt-5.5")]`

**Copilot-cloud confirmation:** copilot's crew hand is `LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` (foreman.rs:210) — a *separate* dispatcher that does not take a model. The `HostCliHandDispatcher` is only ever constructed for codex/opencode/aider (gated by `host_name_for_kind`, foreman.rs:275 returns `None` for copilot/claude). So `auto` on a copilot binding never reaches a tiered selection — `host_name_for_kind(Copilot)==None` means the host-CLI branch is skipped and copilot's own dispatcher runs. **`auto` + copilot → copilot dispatcher, model ignored, correct by construction.** No `None`-tier handling needed in the catalogue for copilot.

---

## Point 4 — `auto` sentinel end-to-end

Introduce a `ModelChoice` derived from the RAW model string, parsed at the **edge** (where `def.model()` is read), so the config layer stays a dumb string store and validation stays tolerant.

```rust
// New: crates/derrick-tools/src/catalogue.rs (or a small new module reachable by hand + cli)
pub enum ModelChoice {
    Pinned(String),                 // concrete id -> always wins
    Auto { bias: Option<Tier> },    // "auto" | "auto:light" | "auto:heavy"
}
pub fn parse_model_choice(raw: &str) -> ModelChoice {
    match raw.trim() {
        "auto" => ModelChoice::Auto { bias: None },
        "auto:light" => ModelChoice::Auto { bias: Some(Tier::Light) },
        "auto:heavy" => ModelChoice::Auto { bias: Some(Tier::Heavy) },
        "auto:standard" => ModelChoice::Auto { bias: Some(Tier::Standard) },
        other => ModelChoice::Pinned(other.to_owned()),
    }
}
```
Keep `ModelDef.model` a plain `String` (config layer unchanged — `required(self.model, ...)` at lib.rs:1651 still requires it; `"auto"` satisfies that). **Validation tolerance:**
- `validate_roles` (config lib.rs:1276): unchanged — it only checks the role→model *name* mapping exists, never inspects the id. `auto` passes untouched.
- `models check` (`check_model`, models.rs:151): add an **early return** at the top: `if model_id.trim().starts_with("auto") { return ModelCheck::pass(subject, "auto: foreman selects per-ticket within host `{provider}`"); }`. This stops `auto` being WARNed as an "unknown catalogue id" and stops the opencode/aider `/`-check from flagging it. Place it before the `shell` check.
- **Never pass `--model auto` to a CLI:** guaranteed because selection resolves `Auto` to a concrete id (or `None`) *before* building `HostRequest` (point 5). Add a defensive assert/test that `select_model` never returns `Some("auto")`.

**`hand_kind_for_executor` interaction:** unaffected. It reads `provider` + `cli` (steps.rs:780), never `model`. `auto` lives in `model`, so `provider` still names the host and `HandKind` still resolves. Confirmed safe.

**Default config:** change `("executor","copilot")` (config lib.rs:148) — actually leave the *role→model name* as is, but the *executor model's* `model` field. Today defaults bind `executor → "copilot"` model whose `model: "gpt-5.4"` (lib.rs:133). To make "executor → auto" the default per the locked decision, change the default `copilot` model's `model` to... no — copilot is cloud and ignores model. To demonstrate `auto`, the **default executor binding should point at a host-CLI model** (e.g. a `codex` model) with `model: "auto"`. **Flag for the user:** the current default executor is `copilot` (cloud), where `auto` is a no-op. If they want `auto` to actually drive tier selection, the default executor must bind a codex/opencode/aider model. Recommend: add a default model `executor-auto { provider: "codex", model: "auto" }` and bind `executor → executor-auto`, OR keep copilot default and document that `auto` only activates for host-CLI executors. This is a **product decision** — see Open Questions.

## Point 5 — Per-ticket selection restructure (load-bearing)

Replace `HostCliHandDispatcher.model: Option<String>` (lib.rs:90) with `model_choice: ModelChoice`. Resolve per-ticket inside `dispatch_assigned` (lib.rs:370) right before `request.model` is set (lib.rs:384):

```rust
// crates/derrick-hand/src/lib.rs
pub struct HostCliHandDispatcher {
    // ...
    model_choice: ModelChoice,   // was: model: Option<String>
    // ...
}

fn select_model(&self, ticket: &Ticket) -> Option<String> {
    match &self.model_choice {
        ModelChoice::Pinned(id) => Some(id.clone()),  // PINNED always wins
        ModelChoice::Auto { bias } => {
            let tier = bias.unwrap_or_else(|| match ticket.complexity {
                Some(Complexity::Low) => Tier::Light,
                Some(Complexity::Heavy) => Tier::Heavy,
                Some(Complexity::Standard) | None => Tier::Standard, // None -> Standard default
            });
            derrick_tools::catalogue::builtin()
                .model_for_tier(self.host_name, tier)
                .map(|m| m.to_owned())            // None for copilot (unreachable here) -> CLI default
        }
    }
}
```
Then at lib.rs:384: `request.model = self.select_model(ticket);` (replacing `self.model.clone()`).

**Bias vs complexity precedence:** `auto:heavy` is a hard bias (ignores ticket complexity) per the brief ("bias"). If you want bias to be a *floor* rather than an override, change the `bias` branch — but the brief says "bias to", so treat as override. **Confirm with user** (Open Questions).

**No trait change needed.** `DispatchContext` already carries `ticket: &Ticket` (foreman.rs:198), and once `Ticket` has `complexity`, `ctx.ticket.complexity` is available inside `dispatch_assigned`. `HandDispatcher` trait, `DispatchContext`, `DispatchResult` all **unchanged**. This is the minimal shape.

**Constructor:** `HostCliHandDispatcher::new` takes `model_choice: ModelChoice` instead of `model: Option<String>`. Caller is `build_dispatcher` (foreman.rs:178). `resolve_executor` (foreman.rs:250) currently returns `(HandKind, Option<String>)` — change to `(HandKind, ModelChoice)`: parse `model.model()` via `parse_model_choice` instead of the blank→None logic (the blank-handling becomes: empty string → `ModelChoice::Auto{None}`? No — empty should stay "use CLI default". Map empty → a `Pinned("")`? Better: keep `Option`, return `(HandKind, ModelChoice)` where blank → `ModelChoice::Pinned` is wrong. **Cleanest:** `parse_model_choice` on a blank string returns `ModelChoice::Pinned("")`, and `select_model` maps `Pinned(s) if s.trim().is_empty() => None`. Encode that in `select_model`'s Pinned arm: `Some(id) if !id.trim().is_empty()`.)

## Point 6 — Non-crew path (pipeline `host:` steps)

The pipeline host step (steps.rs:206-221) reads `def.model().trim()` directly and forwards it as `request.model`. With `auto` in the model field, this would forward literal `--model auto` — **a bug**. Fix at steps.rs:213-221: parse the model with `parse_model_choice`; for `Auto`, select the **bias tier if present, else `Tier::Standard`** (no ticket exists at pipeline-step time):

```rust
let model_id = step.role()
    .and_then(|r| config.roles().get(r))
    .and_then(|m| config.models().get(m))
    .and_then(|def| {
        match parse_model_choice(def.model()) {
            ModelChoice::Pinned(id) if !id.trim().is_empty() => Some(id),
            ModelChoice::Pinned(_) => None,
            ModelChoice::Auto { bias } =>
                catalogue::builtin()
                    .model_for_tier(host_name, bias.unwrap_or(Tier::Standard))
                    .map(str::to_owned),
        }
    });
request.model = model_id;
```
This is the single other site that reads a model id and forwards it to a CLI. The `execute_foreman` pipeline step (steps.rs:588-598) reads `model.provider()`/`model.cli()` only for `hand_kind`, never the model id for a CLI — **no change needed there** (it never sets `--model`).

## Point 7 — Blast radius, compile-safe sequence, risks

### Every match/validation/decode site touched
1. `derrick-substrate/src/types.rs` — `Complexity` enum (+FromStr/Display); `Ticket.complexity`; `NewTicket.complexity` (public field, defaulted in `new`).
2. `derrick-substrate-native/migrations/0004_ticket_complexity.sql` — new file.
3. `derrick-substrate-native/src/lib.rs` — `SCHEMA_VERSION=4` (19); `MIGRATION_0004` const; `run_migration_0004`; `migrate()` (1975); INSERT (637); SELECT column lists in `select_optional_ticket` (2296); `ticket_base_from_row` decode (2467).
4. `derrick-tools/src/catalogue.rs` — `Tier`, `ModelChoice`, `parse_model_choice`, `HostModels.tiers`, `model_for_tier`, populate 5 hosts, tests.
5. `derrick-hand/src/lib.rs` — struct field `model_choice` (90); `new` signature (97); `select_model`; `dispatch_assigned` (384); update the 3 test constructors (664, 736, 774) to pass `ModelChoice::Pinned("openai/gpt-5.5".into())`; the test `make_ticket` (524) is unaffected (complexity defaults None).
6. `derrick-cli/src/commands/foreman.rs` — `resolve_executor` return type (250); `build_dispatcher` call (178-185).
7. `derrick-flow/src/steps.rs` — bridge parse (`parse_complexity_marker`, the two `NewTicket` push sites 728/756); pipeline host-step model resolution (213-221); optional log line in `execute_foreman`.
8. `derrick-cli/src/commands/models.rs` — `check_model` early `auto` pass (151).
9. `derrick-config/src/lib.rs` — optionally the default executor binding (148) + a default host-CLI model (product decision).
10. The `/tasks` speckit prompt template (annotate to emit markers) — find under `.specify/` or the speckit skill templates.

### Compile-safe build sequence
1. **derrick-substrate**: add `Complexity` + fields (defaulted in `NewTicket::new`, so no caller breaks). Compiles standalone.
2. **derrick-substrate-native**: migration 0004 + INSERT/SELECT/decode. Compiles against step 1. Run migration tests.
3. **derrick-tools**: `Tier`/`ModelChoice`/`parse_model_choice`/tiers/`model_for_tier`. Pure addition; compiles standalone (catalogue tests updated for new struct field — every `HostModels{..}` literal needs `tiers:`).
4. **derrick-hand**: swap `model` → `model_choice`, add `select_model`, update 3 test ctors. Depends on tools+substrate. Compiles.
5. **derrick-cli/commands/foreman.rs**: `resolve_executor` + `build_dispatcher`. Depends on hand+tools.
6. **derrick-cli/commands/models.rs**: `auto` early-pass.
7. **derrick-flow/steps.rs**: bridge marker parse + pipeline host-step `auto` resolution.
8. **derrick-config**: default binding (last; product-gated).
9. speckit `/tasks` template annotation.
10. fmt + clippy + workspace tests.

Steps 1→4 are each independently compilable. The only cross-crate breakage is the `HostModels` struct literal (step 3 forces updating all 5 entries + tests in the same edit) and `HostCliHandDispatcher::new` (step 4 forces foreman.rs in step 5).

### Risks
- **R1 (high) — tasks-format fragility.** LLM may omit/garble the marker. Mitigated by `None`→Standard fallback (harmless) and permissive parse. Complexity is advisory, never blocking. *Accept.*
- **R2 (low) — migration.** Pure `ADD COLUMN` is safe; the `CHECK` passes because all existing rows are `NULL`. Risk only if a future writer inserts an out-of-enum string — guarded by `Complexity::as_str` being the only writer. Add a migration round-trip test (open v3 db, migrate, insert ticket with each complexity, read back).
- **R3 (medium) — `auto` leaking as a literal `--model auto`.** Two forwarding sites (hand `dispatch_assigned`, pipeline host step). Both must resolve `Auto` before building `HostRequest`. Mitigate with a unit test asserting `select_model` and the pipeline resolver never return `Some("auto")`, and a `check_model` test that `auto` is PASS not WARN.
- **R4 (low) — copilot + auto.** Confirmed inert: `host_name_for_kind(Copilot)==None` skips the host-CLI dispatcher; copilot's own dispatcher ignores model. Add a test that an `executor→auto` bound to `provider: copilot` still builds the copilot dispatcher.
- **R5 (medium) — default-config product gap.** The current default executor is copilot (cloud), where `auto` does nothing. Shipping "default executor → auto" only has teeth if the default executor is a host CLI. Needs a product call (Open Questions).
- **R6 (low) — column index drift in decode.** New `complexity` column appended last (index 11) so existing `row.get(9/10)` for timestamps shift to... they don't shift (complexity goes *after* updated_at in the SELECT). Verify the SELECT column order in `select_optional_ticket` matches `ticket_base_from_row` indices exactly.

---

## Open questions for the user
1. **Default executor host:** keep copilot (cloud) default and make `auto` a no-op there, or change the default executor to a host CLI (codex) so `auto` actually drives tier selection out of the box?
2. **`auto:heavy` semantics:** hard override (ignore ticket complexity) or a floor (max of bias and complexity)? Brief says "bias"; I've designed it as a hard override.
3. **Marker syntax:** HTML comment `<!-- complexity: heavy -->` (my recommendation) vs bracket `## [H] title`? The comment form is more robust but the bracket form is more visible to a human editing `tasks.md`.

# Plan: foreman-driven adaptive model selection (D67)

## Context

Today the crew executor model is a static `derrick.yaml` role→model pin, and the model is the same for every ticket. The user wants: **the user picks the tool (host); the foreman picks the best model within that host per ticket, based on the ticket's size/complexity; an explicit pin in `derrick.yaml` always wins.** This stacks on D65 (host-CLI routing + catalogue) and D66 (host-CLI crew hands + per-ticket worktrees, PR #20).

**Locked decisions:**
1. **Complexity = upstream structured estimate** on the ticket. The `tasks` generation step emits a per-task complexity marker; the tasks→tickets bridge parses it onto a new `Ticket.complexity` field. Missing → treated as `Standard` at selection (never blocks).
2. **Availability = the curated D65 catalogue**, extended with per-host **tiers** (light/standard/heavy).
3. **Override = an `auto` sentinel** in the role's model id: a concrete id is a PIN (always wins); `auto` (or `auto:light`/`auto:heavy`) lets the foreman pick within the host. `auto:*` bias is a **hard override** of the tier (ignores ticket complexity). Default config: executor model = `auto`.

**Correction that shaped the design:** the crew runs **local CLIs** for *all* hosts — including copilot (`LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` spawns the local `copilot` CLI; the cloud/GitHub-issue dispatcher is intentionally not wired). The local copilot CLI accepts `--model` but the dispatcher doesn't pass it today. So copilot is a full tiered host here, not a server-side no-op, and **adaptive selection must reach all three crew CLI dispatchers**: the generic `HostCliHandDispatcher` (codex/opencode/aider), `LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` (copilot), and `ClaudeHandDispatcher` (claude).

This refines D65/D66 and changes a public dispatcher shape across crates → gated on **design-keeper** (record D67, amend §6.5) and **rust-architect** (the per-ticket `ModelChoice` restructure across three dispatchers + the new ticket field/migration). Depends on D66 (PR #20) merging first; branch off #20's head.

## Design

### 1. Complexity on the ticket (`derrick-substrate` + `-native`)
- New `Complexity { Low, Standard, Heavy }` enum in `crates/derrick-substrate/src/types.rs` (snake_case serde, `FromStr`/`Display`, `#[non_exhaustive]`).
- Add `complexity: Option<Complexity>` as a **public field** on `Ticket` and `NewTicket` (default `None` in `NewTicket::new`, so no existing caller breaks — the bridge sets it after construction).
- **Migration `0004`** (`crates/derrick-substrate-native/migrations/0004_ticket_complexity.sql`): a clean `ALTER TABLE tickets ADD COLUMN complexity TEXT NULL CHECK (complexity IS NULL OR complexity IN ('low','standard','heavy'))` — **no table rebuild** (unlike 0003; the new nullable column adds cleanly and the CHECK passes on all-NULL existing rows). Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION=4`, add `run_migration_0004` (plain transactioned `execute_batch`, no FK-off), wire `if version < 4` in `migrate()`. Add `complexity` to the INSERT (lib.rs ~637) and the `select_optional_ticket` SELECT list + `ticket_base_from_row` decode (lib.rs ~2296/2467) — append the column **last** so existing row indices don't shift.

### 2. Producer: tasks step + bridge (`derrick-flow` + speckit template)
- Annotate the `/tasks` generation prompt/template so each task heading carries a trailing marker `<!-- complexity: low|standard|heavy -->` (HTML comment: survives rendering, never collides with the title).
- In the bridge `parse_tasks_from_markdown` (`crates/derrick-flow/src/steps.rs` ~723), a permissive `parse_complexity_marker(title) -> (clean_title, Option<Complexity>)` strips the marker and sets `nt.complexity` at the two `NewTicket` push sites (~728/756). Unknown/missing → `None` (advisory, never errors).

### 3. Catalogue tiers + `ModelChoice` (`derrick-tools/src/catalogue.rs`)
- `enum Tier { Light, Standard, Heavy }`; add `tiers: &'static [(Tier, &'static str)]` (ordered, may be empty) to `HostModels`; `model_for_tier(host, tier) -> Option<&'static str>` (exact tier → else `default_model` → else last tier).
- Populate all five hosts, e.g.: claude `haiku-4-5 / sonnet-4-6 / opus-4-8`; codex `gpt-5.4-mini / gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.5`; **copilot `claude-haiku-4.5 / gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.3-codex`**; opencode/aider with their `provider/model` ids.
- `enum ModelChoice { Pinned(String), Auto { bias: Option<Tier> } }` + `parse_model_choice(raw)` (`auto`/`auto:light`/`auto:standard`/`auto:heavy` → `Auto`; else `Pinned`).
- Shared `select_model(catalogue, host, choice, ticket_complexity) -> Option<String>`: `Pinned(non-empty)` → that id; `Pinned(empty)` → `None`; `Auto{bias}` → `model_for_tier(host, bias.unwrap_or(complexity→tier; None→Standard))`. **Guarantee it never returns `Some("auto")`** (defended by test).

### 4. Per-ticket selection in the three crew dispatchers
Each gains a `model_choice: ModelChoice` (replacing/adding to a fixed model) and resolves **per ticket** via `select_model(.., ctx.ticket.complexity)` immediately before invoking its CLI:
- `crates/derrick-hand/src/lib.rs` `HostCliHandDispatcher`: swap `model: Option<String>` → `model_choice`; set `request.model = select_model(...)` in `dispatch_assigned`.
- `crates/derrick-copilot/src/local_dispatcher.rs`: add `model_choice`; pass `--model <selected>` to the `copilot -p …` spawn (~line 369) when `Some`. (add `derrick-tools` dep)
- `crates/derrick-claude/src/dispatcher.rs`: add `model_choice`; pass `--model <selected>` to the `claude --print` spawn when `Some`. (add `derrick-tools` dep)
- `DispatchContext` already carries `ticket: &Ticket` → no trait change.

### 5. Foreman wiring (`derrick-cli/src/commands/foreman.rs`)
- `resolve_executor` returns `(HandKind, ModelChoice)` (parse `ModelDef.model()` via `parse_model_choice`).
- In `build_dispatcher`, attach that `ModelChoice` to whichever dispatcher matches the executor's `HandKind` (generic / local-copilot / claude); the others default to `ModelChoice::Auto{None}` or a sensible pin.

### 6. `auto` tolerance + non-crew path
- `derrick-cli/src/commands/models.rs` `check_model`: early-PASS when the id starts with `auto` ("foreman selects per-ticket within host `<provider>`") — before the catalogue/`/`-shape checks, so `auto` is never WARNed and never sent as a literal `--model auto`.
- Config validation unchanged (`validate_roles` checks the name mapping only; `ModelDef.model` stays required, `"auto"` satisfies it).
- Pipeline `host:` steps (D66 Part A, `steps.rs` ~213): resolve the model via `parse_model_choice`; `Auto` → `model_for_tier(host, bias.unwrap_or(Standard))` (no ticket at pipeline time). Never forward literal `auto`.

### 7. Default config (`derrick-config`)
- Default the executor model id to `auto` (keep executor host = copilot). Adaptive selection is then on by default and works because the local copilot CLI takes `--model`.

## Critical files
- `crates/derrick-substrate/src/types.rs` (Complexity, Ticket/NewTicket field)
- `crates/derrick-substrate-native/{migrations/0004_ticket_complexity.sql, src/lib.rs}` (migration + INSERT/SELECT/decode)
- `crates/derrick-tools/src/catalogue.rs` (Tier, tiers, model_for_tier, ModelChoice, parse_model_choice, select_model)
- `crates/derrick-hand/src/lib.rs`, `crates/derrick-copilot/src/local_dispatcher.rs`, `crates/derrick-claude/src/dispatcher.rs` (per-ticket model_choice + `--model`)
- `crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/{foreman.rs, models.rs}` (resolve_executor → ModelChoice; auto pass)
- `crates/derrick-flow/src/steps.rs` (bridge marker parse; pipeline-step auto resolution)
- `crates/derrick-config/src/lib.rs` (default executor model = auto)
- speckit `/tasks` template (emit the complexity marker)

## Build sequence (compiles at each step)
1. `derrick-substrate`: Complexity + fields (defaulted). 2. `-native`: migration 0004 + INSERT/SELECT/decode + round-trip test. 3. `derrick-tools`: Tier/tiers/model_for_tier/ModelChoice/parse_model_choice/select_model + update all 5 `HostModels` literals + tests. 4. `derrick-hand`: model_choice + select. 5. `derrick-copilot` + `derrick-claude`: add derrick-tools dep, model_choice, `--model`. 6. `derrick-cli` foreman + models. 7. `derrick-flow` bridge + pipeline path. 8. `derrick-config` default. 9. speckit template. 10. fmt + clippy + tests.

## Verification
- Unit: `parse_model_choice` (auto variants vs pin); `select_model` per (host, complexity, bias) incl. **never returns `Some("auto")`** and empty-pin → `None`; `model_for_tier` fallbacks; `parse_complexity_marker` per marker shape.
- Migration: open a v3 DB, migrate to v4, insert tickets with each `Complexity` + read back; FK/`foreign_key_check` clean.
- Dispatchers: per-dispatcher test (stub CLI/adapter capturing args) that a `Heavy` ticket + `auto` yields the host's heavy-tier `--model`, a `Low` ticket the light-tier, a pin always wins, and copilot now receives `--model`.
- `models check`: `auto` and `auto:heavy` → PASS (not WARN/FAIL).
- E2E: a `derrick.yaml` with `executor` model `auto` on an opencode/codex/copilot host; run the foreman against tickets of differing complexity; assert differing `--model` per ticket; then pin a concrete model and assert it overrides.
- `cargo fmt` + `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` + `cargo test --workspace` green.

## Risks
- **Tasks-marker fragility** (LLM omits/garbles): mitigated by `None`→Standard fallback + permissive parse; complexity is advisory.
- **`auto` leaking as literal `--model auto`**: two forwarding sites (hand dispatchers, pipeline step) + `models check`; covered by the "never returns `auto`" guarantee + tests.
- **Migration on `tickets`**: pure ADD COLUMN is safe (verified no rebuild needed); round-trip test guards it.
- **Three-dispatcher surface**: the `--model` + `model_choice` change repeats across generic/copilot/claude dispatchers; a shared `select_model` keeps the logic single-sourced. (rust-architect to confirm whether folding the copilot/claude dispatchers onto the generic path is preferable — deferred unless cheap.)

## Gates & ownership
design-keeper records **D67** (foreman adaptive model selection; tiers; `auto` sentinel; complexity field) and amends §6.5 → rust-architect ratifies the `ModelChoice` restructure across the three dispatchers + the ticket field/migration → substrate-engineer (field/migration/foreman) + integrations-engineer (catalogue/select_model/dispatcher `--model`) implement → Codex review → PR stacked on / rebased after D66 (#20).

# Plan: foreman-driven adaptive model selection (D67)

## Context

Today the crew executor model is a static `derrick.yaml` role→model pin, and the model is the same for every ticket. The user wants: **the user picks the tool (host); the foreman picks the best model within that host per ticket, based on the ticket's size/complexity; an explicit pin in `derrick.yaml` always wins.** This stacks on D65 (host-CLI routing + catalogue) and D66 (host-CLI crew hands + per-ticket worktrees, PR #20).

**Locked decisions:**
1. **Complexity = upstream structured estimate** on the ticket. The `tasks` generation step emits a per-task complexity marker; the tasks→tickets bridge parses it onto a new `Ticket.complexity` field. Missing → treated as `Standard` at selection (never blocks).
2. **Availability = the curated D65 catalogue**, extended with per-host **tiers** (light/standard/heavy).
3. **Override = an `auto` sentinel** in the role's model id: a concrete id is a PIN (always wins); `auto` (or `auto:light`/`auto:heavy`) lets the foreman pick within the host. `auto:*` bias is a **hard override** of the tier (ignores ticket complexity). Default config: executor model = `auto`.

**Correction that shaped the design:** the crew runs **local CLIs** for *all* hosts — including copilot (`LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` spawns the local `copilot` CLI; the cloud/GitHub-issue dispatcher is intentionally not wired). The local copilot CLI accepts `--model` but the dispatcher doesn't pass it today. So copilot is a full tiered host here, not a server-side no-op, and **adaptive selection must reach all three crew CLI dispatchers**: the generic `HostCliHandDispatcher` (codex/opencode/aider), `LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` (copilot), and `ClaudeHandDispatcher` (claude).

This refines D65/D66 and changes a public dispatcher shape across crates → gated on **design-keeper** (record D67, amend §6.5) and **rust-architect** (the per-ticket `ModelChoice` restructure across three dispatchers + the new ticket field/migration). Depends on D66 (PR #20) merging first; branch off #20's head.

### 1. Complexity on the ticket (`derrick-substrate` + `-native`)

Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION=4`, add `run_migration_0004` (plain transactioned `execute_batch`, no FK-off), wire `if version < 4` in `migrate()`. ### 2. Producer: tasks step + bridge (`derrick-flow` + speckit template)
- Annotate the `/tasks` generation prompt/template so each task heading carries a trailing marker `<!-- complexity: low|standard|heavy -->` (HTML comment: survives rendering, never collides with the title).

### 3. Catalogue tiers + `ModelChoice` (`derrick-tools/src/catalogue.rs`)

- `DispatchContext` already carries `ticket: &Ticket` → no trait change.

### 5. Foreman wiring (`derrick-cli/src/commands/foreman.rs`)
- `resolve_executor` returns `(HandKind, ModelChoice)` (parse `ModelDef.model()` via `parse_model_choice`).

### 7. Default config (`derrick-config`)
- Default the executor model id to `auto` (keep executor host = copilot). Adaptive selection is then on by default and works because the local copilot CLI takes `--model`.

## Critical files

- `crates/derrick-substrate-native/{migrations/0004_ticket_complexity.sql, src/lib.rs}` (migration + INSERT/SELECT/decode)
- `crates/derrick-tools/src/catalogue.rs` (Tier, tiers, model_for_tier, ModelChoice, parse_model_choice, select_model)
- `crates/derrick-hand/src/lib.rs`, `crates/derrick-copilot/src/local_dispatcher.rs`, `crates/derrick-claude/src/dispatcher.rs` (per-ticket model_choice + `--model`)
- `crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/{foreman.rs, models.rs}` (resolve_executor → ModelChoice; auto pass)
- `crates/derrick-flow/src/steps.rs` (bridge marker parse; pipeline-step auto resolution)

Today the crew executor model is a static `derrick.yaml` role→model pin, and the model is the same for every ticket. Add `complexity` to the INSERT (lib.rs ~637) and the `select_optional_ticket` SELECT list + `ticket_base_from_row` decode (lib.rs ~2296/2467) — append the column **last** so existing row indices don't shift.

### 2. Producer: tasks step + bridge (`derrick-flow` + speckit template)
- Annotate the `/tasks` generation prompt/template so each task heading carries a trailing marker `<!-- complexity: low|standard|heavy -->` (HTML comment: survives rendering, never collides with the title).
- In the bridge `parse_tasks_from_markdown` (`crates/derrick-flow/src/steps.rs` ~723), a permissive `parse_complexity_marker(title) -> (clean_title, Option<Complexity>)` strips the marker and sets `nt.complexity` at the two `NewTicket` push sites (~728/756). Unknown/missing → `None` (advisory, never errors).

### 3. Catalogue tiers + `ModelChoice` (`derrick-tools/src/catalogue.rs`)
- `enum Tier { Light, Standard, Heavy }`; add `tiers: &'static [(Tier, &'static str)]` (ordered, may be empty) to `HostModels`; `model_for_tier(host, tier) -> Option<&'static str>` (exact tier → else `default_model` → else last tier).
- Populate all five hosts, e.g.: claude `haiku-4-5 / sonnet-4-6 / opus-4-8`; codex `gpt-5.4-mini / gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.5`; **copilot `claude-haiku-4.5 / gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.3-codex`**; opencode/aider with their `provider/model` ids.
- `enum ModelChoice { Pinned(String), Auto { bias: Option<Tier> } }` + `parse_model_choice(raw)` (`auto`/`auto:light`/`auto:standard`/`auto:heavy` → `Auto`; else `Pinned`).
- Shared `select_model(catalogue, host, choice, ticket_complexity) -> Option<String>`: `Pinned(non-empty)` → that id; `Pinned(empty)` → `None`; `Auto{bias}` → `model_for_tier(host, bias.unwrap_or(complexity→tier; None→Standard))`. **Guarantee it never returns `Some("auto")`** (defended by test).

### 4. Per-ticket selection in the three crew dispatchers
Each gains a `model_choice: ModelChoice` (replacing/adding to a fixed model) and resolves **per ticket** via `select_model(.., ctx.ticket.complexity)` immediately before invoking its CLI:
- `crates/derrick-hand/src/lib.rs` `HostCliHandDispatcher`: swap `model: Option<String>` → `model_choice`; set `request.model = select_model(...)` in `dispatch_assigned`.
- `crates/derrick-copilot/src/local_dispatcher.rs`: add `model_choice`; pass `--model <selected>` to the `copilot -p …` spawn (~line 369) when `Some`. (add `derrick-tools` dep)
- `crates/derrick-claude/src/dispatcher.rs`: add `model_choice`; pass `--model <selected>` to the `claude --print` spawn when `Some`. (add `derrick-tools` dep)
- `DispatchContext` already carries `ticket: &Ticket` → no trait change.

### 5. Foreman wiring (`derrick-cli/src/commands/foreman.rs`)
- `resolve_executor` returns `(HandKind, ModelChoice)` (parse `ModelDef.model()` via `parse_model_choice`).
- In `build_dispatcher`, attach that `ModelChoice` to whichever dispatcher matches the executor's `HandKind` (generic / local-copilot / claude); the others default to `ModelChoice::Auto{None}` or a sensible pin.

### 6. `auto` tolerance + non-crew path
- `derrick-cli/src/commands/models.rs` `check_model`: early-PASS when the id starts with `auto` ("foreman selects per-ticket within host `<provider>`") — before the catalogue/`/`-shape checks, so `auto` is never WARNed and never sent as a literal `--model auto`.
- Config validation unchanged (`validate_roles` checks the name mapping only; `ModelDef.model` stays required, `"auto"` satisfies it).
- Pipeline `host:` steps (D66 Part A, `steps.rs` ~213): resolve the model via `parse_model_choice`; `Auto` → `model_for_tier(host, bias.unwrap_or(Standard))` (no ticket at pipeline time). Never forward literal `auto`.

### 7. Default config (`derrick-config`)
- Default the executor model id to `auto` (keep executor host = copilot). Adaptive selection is then on by default and works because the local copilot CLI takes `--model`.

- `crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/{foreman.rs, models.rs}` (resolve_executor → ModelChoice; auto pass)

## Build sequence (compiles at each step)
1. `derrick-substrate`: Complexity + fields (defaulted). 2. `-native`: migration 0004 + INSERT/SELECT/decode + round-trip test. 3. `derrick-tools`: Tier/tiers/model_for_tier/ModelChoice/parse_model_choice/select_model + update all 5 `HostModels` literals + tests. 4. `derrick-hand`: model_choice + select. 5. `derrick-copilot` + `derrick-claude`: add derrick-tools dep, model_choice, `--model`. 6. `derrick-cli` foreman + models. 7. `derrick-flow` bridge + pipeline path. 8. `derrick-config` default. 9. speckit template. 10. fmt + clippy + tests.

## Verification
- Unit: `parse_model_choice` (auto variants vs pin); `select_model` per (host, complexity, bias) incl. **never returns `Some("auto")`** and empty-pin → `None`; `model_for_tier` fallbacks; `parse_complexity_marker` per marker shape.
- Migration: open a v3 DB, migrate to v4, insert tickets with each `Complexity` + read back; FK/`foreign_key_check` clean.
- Dispatchers: per-dispatcher test (stub CLI/adapter capturing args) that a `Heavy` ticket + `auto` yields the host's heavy-tier `--model`, a `Low` ticket the light-tier, a pin always wins, and copilot now receives `--model`.
- `models check`: `auto` and `auto:heavy` → PASS (not WARN/FAIL).
- E2E: a `derrick.yaml` with `executor` model `auto` on an opencode/codex/copilot host; run the foreman against tickets of differing complexity; assert differing `--model` per ticket; then pin a concrete model and assert it overrides.
- `cargo fmt` + `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` + `cargo test --workspace` green.

## Risks
- **Tasks-marker fragility** (LLM omits/garbles): mitigated by `None`→Standard fallback + permissive parse; complexity is advisory.
- **`auto` leaking as literal `--model auto`**: two forwarding sites (hand dispatchers, pipeline step) + `models check`; covered by the "never returns `auto`" guarantee + tests.
- **Migration on `tickets`**: pure ADD COLUMN is safe (verified no rebuild needed); round-trip test guards it.
- **Three-dispatcher surface**: the `--model` + `model_choice` change repeats across generic/copilot/claude dispatchers; a shared `select_model` keeps the logic single-sourced. (rust-architect to confirm whether folding the copilot/claude dispatchers onto the generic path is preferable — deferred unless cheap.)

## Context

derrick today conflates two things and lets inference escape the host CLIs:

- `derrick-models` ships a **direct-API** `anthropic` provider (reqwest + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) plus an `openai-cli` provider with an API-key mode — i.e. it can call model APIs directly with user keys (BYOM, D12 / §6.5).
- The default model IDs are **stale**: config has `claude-opus-4-7`, `gpt-5`, `gpt-5-codex`; reality (May 2026) is Opus 4.8 / Sonnet 4.6 / Haiku 4.5, Codex `gpt-5.5`/`gpt-5.4`/`gpt-5.2-codex`, Copilot `gpt-5.4`/`gpt-5.3-codex`/`claude-sonnet-4.6`.
- Host adapters forward `--model` **verbatim** with no per-host normalisation, even though codex/copilot want a bare id (`gpt-5.5`) while opencode/aider want `provider/model`.
- `aider` is not supported at all; the `copilot-cli` provider named in `Config::defaults()` is **never registered** (latent `UnknownProvider` bug — the executor role only works via the host path, not the Model path).

**Desired outcome:** every model role resolves to exactly one of **5 host CLIs** — `claude`, `codex`, `copilot`, `opencode`, `aider` — which each manage their own auth. derrick holds no API keys. Anthropic models run via Claude Code, OpenAI via Codex, and copilot/opencode/aider authenticate themselves. Model choices are validated against a curated, current list (warn-and-pass-through on unknowns).

**User decisions (confirmed):**
1. **Host-CLI only** — delete direct-API providers + API-key/credential machinery; supersede **D12**, rewrite **§6.5**.
2. **Hybrid validation** — curated current model IDs drive defaults + `derrick models check`; unknown models **warn** and still pass through.
3. **aider is a first-class host adapter**, all auth delegated to aider's own config.
4. (Implied by "support these 5") opencode and aider become **first-class pipeline hosts** — the `Host` enum gains `Opencode` and `Aider`, not role-path reachability.

This crosses crate boundaries, contradicts a recorded decision, and renames public provider identifiers, so it is gated on a **design-keeper** decision entry and a **rust-architect** sign-off on the new `derrick-models → derrick-tools` dependency before implementation.

## Target architecture

- **One subprocess layer.** `derrick-tools` host adapters remain the only place that shells out to a CLI. `derrick-models` gains a dependency on `derrick-tools` (no cycle — tools is a leaf) and its CLI providers collapse into a **single host-delegated provider** that maps a `ModelDef` → host + model, builds a `HostRequest`, calls the adapter's `run()`, and wraps the one `HostResponse` into a one-shot `CompletionStream` (`Content` then `End{tokens}`). This satisfies the only completion consumers (`derrick-assay`, `derrick-flow/code_review`) which call `.complete()`, and gives them real token counts for free.
- **Curated catalogue** owned by `derrick-tools` (new `src/catalogue.rs`): host id → `{ default_model, known: [...], id_style: BareId | ProviderModel }`. Single source of truth for defaults, `models check`, and normalisation. Reachable by both the adapters and the CLI without a cycle.
- **Per-host model normalisation** applied inside each adapter before pushing `--model`: claude strips a leading `anthropic/`; codex strips `openai/`; copilot strips any `provider/` prefix (keeps its own dotted ids — do **not** translate dot↔dash); opencode/aider pass `provider/model` through verbatim.
- **No BYOK:** `AuthStore` shrinks to env-passthrough only (still needed — `HostRequest.env` is forwarded to the child, e.g. `GH_TOKEN`/proxy vars). `require()`/`missing_required()`/`required` field and `ModelError::MissingCredential` are removed. `reqwest` drops out of `derrick-models`.
- **`shell` provider survives** untouched — it's a bespoke-envelope escape hatch, not a host CLI.

# Plan: foreman-driven adaptive model selection (D67)

## Context

Today the crew executor model is a static `derrick.yaml` role→model pin, and the model is the same for every ticket. The user wants: **the user picks the tool (host); the foreman picks the best model within that host per ticket, based on the ticket's size/complexity; an explicit pin in `derrick.yaml` always wins.** This stacks on D65 (host-CLI routing + catalogue) and D66 (host-CLI crew hands + per-ticket worktrees, PR #20).

**Locked decisions:**
1. **Complexity = upstream structured estimate** on the ticket. The `tasks` generation step emits a per-task complexity marker; the tasks→tickets bridge parses it onto a new `Ticket.complexity` field. Missing → treated as `Standard` at selection (never blocks).
2. **Availability = the curated D65 catalogue**, extended with per-host **tiers** (light/standard/heavy).
3. **Override = an `auto` sentinel** in the role's model id: a concrete id is a PIN (always wins); `auto` (or `auto:light`/`auto:heavy`) lets the foreman pick within the host. `auto:*` bias is a **hard override** of the tier (ignores ticket complexity). Default config: executor model = `auto`.

**Correction that shaped the design:** the crew runs **local CLIs** for *all* hosts — including copilot (`LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` spawns the local `copilot` CLI; the cloud/GitHub-issue dispatcher is intentionally not wired). The local copilot CLI accepts `--model` but the dispatcher doesn't pass it today. So copilot is a full tiered host here, not a server-side no-op, and **adaptive selection must reach all three crew CLI dispatchers**: the generic `HostCliHandDispatcher` (codex/opencode/aider), `LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` (copilot), and `ClaudeHandDispatcher` (claude).

This refines D65/D66 and changes a public dispatcher shape across crates → gated on **design-keeper** (record D67, amend §6.5) and **rust-architect** (the per-ticket `ModelChoice` restructure across three dispatchers + the new ticket field/migration). Depends on D66 (PR #20) merging first; branch off #20's head.

## Design

### 1. Complexity on the ticket (`derrick-substrate` + `-native`)
- New `Complexity { Low, Standard, Heavy }` enum in `crates/derrick-substrate/src/types.rs` (snake_case serde, `FromStr`/`Display`, `#[non_exhaustive]`).
- Add `complexity: Option<Complexity>` as a **public field** on `Ticket` and `NewTicket` (default `None` in `NewTicket::new`, so no existing caller breaks — the bridge sets it after construction).
- **Migration `0004`** (`crates/derrick-substrate-native/migrations/0004_ticket_complexity.sql`): a clean `ALTER TABLE tickets ADD COLUMN complexity TEXT NULL CHECK (complexity IS NULL OR complexity IN ('low','standard','heavy'))` — **no table rebuild** (unlike 0003; the new nullable column adds cleanly and the CHECK passes on all-NULL existing rows). Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION=4`, add `run_migration_0004` (plain transactioned `execute_batch`, no FK-off), wire `if version < 4` in `migrate()`. Add `complexity` to the INSERT (lib.rs ~637) and the `select_optional_ticket` SELECT list + `ticket_base_from_row` decode (lib.rs ~2296/2467) — append the column **last** so existing row indices don't shift.

### 2. Producer: tasks step + bridge (`derrick-flow` + speckit template)
- Annotate the `/tasks` generation prompt/template so each task heading carries a trailing marker `<!-- complexity: low|standard|heavy -->` (HTML comment: survives rendering, never collides with the title).
- In the bridge `parse_tasks_from_markdown` (`crates/derrick-flow/src/steps.rs` ~723), a permissive `parse_complexity_marker(title) -> (clean_title, Option<Complexity>)` strips the marker and sets `nt.complexity` at the two `NewTicket` push sites (~728/756). Unknown/missing → `None` (advisory, never errors).

### 3. Catalogue tiers + `ModelChoice` (`derrick-tools/src/catalogue.rs`)
- `enum Tier { Light, Standard, Heavy }`; add `tiers: &'static [(Tier, &'static str)]` (ordered, may be empty) to `HostModels`; `model_for_tier(host, tier) -> Option<&'static str>` (exact tier → else `default_model` → else last tier).
- Populate all five hosts, e.g.: claude `haiku-4-5 / sonnet-4-6 / opus-4-8`; codex `gpt-5.4-mini / gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.5`; **copilot `claude-haiku-4.5 / gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.3-codex`**; opencode/aider with their `provider/model` ids.
- `enum ModelChoice { Pinned(String), Auto { bias: Option<Tier> } }` + `parse_model_choice(raw)` (`auto`/`auto:light`/`auto:standard`/`auto:heavy` → `Auto`; else `Pinned`).
- Shared `select_model(catalogue, host, choice, ticket_complexity) -> Option<String>`: `Pinned(non-empty)` → that id; `Pinned(empty)` → `None`; `Auto{bias}` → `model_for_tier(host, bias.unwrap_or(complexity→tier; None→Standard))`. **Guarantee it never returns `Some("auto")`** (defended by test).

### 4. Per-ticket selection in the three crew dispatchers
Each gains a `model_choice: ModelChoice` (replacing/adding to a fixed model) and resolves **per ticket** via `select_model(.., ctx.ticket.complexity)` immediately before invoking its CLI:
- `crates/derrick-hand/src/lib.rs` `HostCliHandDispatcher`: swap `model: Option<String>` → `model_choice`; set `request.model = select_model(...)` in `dispatch_assigned`.
- `crates/derrick-copilot/src/local_dispatcher.rs`: add `model_choice`; pass `--model <selected>` to the `copilot -p …` spawn (~line 369) when `Some`. (add `derrick-tools` dep)
- `crates/derrick-claude/src/dispatcher.rs`: add `model_choice`; pass `--model <selected>` to the `claude --print` spawn when `Some`. (add `derrick-tools` dep)
- `DispatchContext` already carries `ticket: &Ticket` → no trait change.

### 5. Foreman wiring (`derrick-cli/src/commands/foreman.rs`)
- `resolve_executor` returns `(HandKind, ModelChoice)` (parse `ModelDef.model()` via `parse_model_choice`).
- In `build_dispatcher`, attach that `ModelChoice` to whichever dispatcher matches the executor's `HandKind` (generic / local-copilot / claude); the others default to `ModelChoice::Auto{None}` or a sensible pin.

### 6. `auto` tolerance + non-crew path
- `derrick-cli/src/commands/models.rs` `check_model`: early-PASS when the id starts with `auto` ("foreman selects per-ticket within host `<provider>`") — before the catalogue/`/`-shape checks, so `auto` is never WARNed and never sent as a literal `--model auto`.
- Config validation unchanged (`validate_roles` checks the name mapping only; `ModelDef.model` stays required, `"auto"` satisfies it).
- Pipeline `host:` steps (D66 Part A, `steps.rs` ~213): resolve the model via `parse_model_choice`; `Auto` → `model_for_tier(host, bias.unwrap_or(Standard))` (no ticket at pipeline time). Never forward literal `auto`.

### 7. Default config (`derrick-config`)
- Default the executor model id to `auto` (keep executor host = copilot). Adaptive selection is then on by default and works because the local copilot CLI takes `--model`.

## Critical files
- `crates/derrick-substrate/src/types.rs` (Complexity, Ticket/NewTicket field)
- `crates/derrick-substrate-native/{migrations/0004_ticket_complexity.sql, src/lib.rs}` (migration + INSERT/SELECT/decode)
- `crates/derrick-tools/src/catalogue.rs` (Tier, tiers, model_for_tier, ModelChoice, parse_model_choice, select_model)
- `crates/derrick-hand/src/lib.rs`, `crates/derrick-copilot/src/local_dispatcher.rs`, `crates/derrick-claude/src/dispatcher.rs` (per-ticket model_choice + `--model`)
- `crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/{foreman.rs, models.rs}` (resolve_executor → ModelChoice; auto pass)
- `crates/derrick-flow/src/steps.rs` (bridge marker parse; pipeline-step auto resolution)
- `crates/derrick-config/src/lib.rs` (default executor model = auto)
- speckit `/tasks` template (emit the complexity marker)

## Build sequence (compiles at each step)
1. `derrick-substrate`: Complexity + fields (defaulted). 2. `-native`: migration 0004 + INSERT/SELECT/decode + round-trip test. 3. `derrick-tools`: Tier/tiers/model_for_tier/ModelChoice/parse_model_choice/select_model + update all 5 `HostModels` literals + tests. 4. `derrick-hand`: model_choice + select. 5. `derrick-copilot` + `derrick-claude`: add derrick-tools dep, model_choice, `--model`. 6. `derrick-cli` foreman + models. 7. `derrick-flow` bridge + pipeline path. 8. `derrick-config` default. 9. speckit template. 10. fmt + clippy + tests.

## Verification
- Unit: `parse_model_choice` (auto variants vs pin); `select_model` per (host, complexity, bias) incl. **never returns `Some("auto")`** and empty-pin → `None`; `model_for_tier` fallbacks; `parse_complexity_marker` per marker shape.
- Migration: open a v3 DB, migrate to v4, insert tickets with each `Complexity` + read back; FK/`foreign_key_check` clean.
- Dispatchers: per-dispatcher test (stub CLI/adapter capturing args) that a `Heavy` ticket + `auto` yields the host's heavy-tier `--model`, a `Low` ticket the light-tier, a pin always wins, and copilot now receives `--model`.
- `models check`: `auto` and `auto:heavy` → PASS (not WARN/FAIL).
- E2E: a `derrick.yaml` with `executor` model `auto` on an opencode/codex/copilot host; run the foreman against tickets of differing complexity; assert differing `--model` per ticket; then pin a concrete model and assert it overrides.

# Plan: foreman-driven adaptive model selection (D67)

## Context

Today the crew executor model is a static `derrick.yaml` role→model pin, and the model is the same for every ticket. The user wants: **the user picks the tool (host); the foreman picks the best model within that host per ticket, based on the ticket's size/complexity; an explicit pin in `derrick.yaml` always wins.** This stacks on D65 (host-CLI routing + catalogue) and D66 (host-CLI crew hands + per-ticket worktrees, PR #20).

**Locked decisions:**
1. **Complexity = upstream structured estimate** on the ticket. The `tasks` generation step emits a per-task complexity marker; the tasks→tickets bridge parses it onto a new `Ticket.complexity` field. Missing → treated as `Standard` at selection (never blocks).
2. **Availability = the curated D65 catalogue**, extended with per-host **tiers** (light/standard/heavy).
3. **Override = an `auto` sentinel** in the role's model id: a concrete id is a PIN (always wins); `auto` (or `auto:light`/`auto:heavy`) lets the foreman pick within the host. `auto:*` bias is a **hard override** of the tier (ignores ticket complexity). Default config: executor model = `auto`.

**Correction that shaped the design:** the crew runs **local CLIs** for *all* hosts — including copilot (`LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` spawns the local `copilot` CLI; the cloud/GitHub-issue dispatcher is intentionally not wired). The local copilot CLI accepts `--model` but the dispatcher doesn't pass it today. So copilot is a full tiered host here, not a server-side no-op, and **adaptive selection must reach all three crew CLI dispatchers**: the generic `HostCliHandDispatcher` (codex/opencode/aider), `LocalCopilotHandDispatcher` (copilot), and `ClaudeHandDispatcher` (claude).

This refines D65/D66 and changes a public dispatcher shape across crates → gated on **design-keeper** (record D67, amend §6.5) and **rust-architect** (the per-ticket `ModelChoice` restructure across three dispatchers + the new ticket field/migration). Depends on D66 (PR #20) merging first; branch off #20's head.

## Design

### 1. Complexity on the ticket (`derrick-substrate` + `-native`)
- New `Complexity { Low, Standard, Heavy }` enum in `crates/derrick-substrate/src/types.rs` (snake_case serde, `FromStr`/`Display`, `#[non_exhaustive]`).
- Add `complexity: Option<Complexity>` as a **public field** on `Ticket` and `NewTicket` (default `None` in `NewTicket::new`, so no existing caller breaks — the bridge sets it after construction).
- **Migration `0004`** (`crates/derrick-substrate-native/migrations/0004_ticket_complexity.sql`): a clean `ALTER TABLE tickets ADD COLUMN complexity TEXT NULL CHECK (complexity IS NULL OR complexity IN ('low','standard','heavy'))` — **no table rebuild** (unlike 0003; the new nullable column adds cleanly and the CHECK passes on all-NULL existing rows). Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION=4`, add `run_migration_0004` (plain transactioned `execute_batch`, no FK-off), wire `if version < 4` in `migrate()`. Add `complexity` to the INSERT (lib.rs ~637) and the `select_optional_ticket` SELECT list + `ticket_base_from_row` decode (lib.rs ~2296/2467) — append the column **last** so existing row indices don't shift.

### 2. Producer: tasks step + bridge (`derrick-flow` + speckit template)
- Annotate the `/tasks` generation prompt/template so each task heading carries a trailing marker `<!-- complexity: low|standard|heavy -->` (HTML comment: survives rendering, never collides with the title).
- In the bridge `parse_tasks_from_markdown` (`crates/derrick-flow/src/steps.rs` ~723), a permissive `parse_complexity_marker(title) -> (clean_title, Option<Complexity>)` strips the marker and sets `nt.complexity` at the two `NewTicket` push sites (~728/756). Unknown/missing → `None` (advisory, never errors).

### 3. Catalogue tiers + `ModelChoice` (`derrick-tools/src/catalogue.rs`)

- Populate all five hosts, e.g.: claude `haiku-4-5 / sonnet-4-6 / opus-4-8`; codex `gpt-5.4-mini / gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.5`; **copilot `claude-haiku-4.5 / gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.3-codex`**; opencode/aider with their `provider/model` ids.

---

# D67 Rust shape — ratified, with one binding correction

The plan is sound and compiles in its build order, with **one decision I'm overruling on dependency grounds** (item 1) and **two small correctness fixes** (items 1 and 6). Everything else stands.

## 1. Shared `ModelChoice` + `select_model` — placement and the `Complexity` seam

**Home: `derrick-tools` is correct.** I verified the graph:
- `derrick-substrate/Cargo.toml` depends on `derrick-config` only — **not** `derrick-tools`. So `derrick-tools` is free to depend on `derrick-substrate` without a cycle *in principle*.
- `derrick-copilot` and `derrick-claude` do **not** currently depend on `derrick-tools`; adding a path dep is clean (neither is in tools' dep tree). `derrick-hand`, `derrick-cli`, `derrick-flow` already depend on `derrick-tools`.

**Binding decision — `select_model` must NOT take `Complexity`.** Keep `derrick-tools` free of any `derrick-substrate` dep. Reasons:
- `derrick-tools` is the designated leaf catalogue crate (its own module doc calls it "single source of truth … without a cycle"). Pulling `derrick-substrate` (which drags `derrick-config`, `chrono`, `uuid`) into the leaf to import a 3-variant enum is the wrong direction of dependency — the substrate type would leak into the model catalogue's public API.
- The `Complexity → Tier` map is trivial and total (`Low→Light`, `Standard→Standard`, `Heavy→Heavy`). It does not belong in tools.

So: **`select_model` takes a resolved `Tier`, not a `Complexity`.** Each dispatcher maps `ticket.complexity` → `Tier` locally (one helper in `derrick-substrate`, see item 2). Final signatures in `derrick-tools/src/catalogue.rs`:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum Tier { Light, Standard, Heavy }

// New field on HostModels (ordered, may be empty):
//   pub tiers: &'static [(Tier, &'static str)],

impl HostModels {
    pub fn model_for_tier(&self, tier: Tier) -> Option<&'static str>;
    // exact tier match → else self.default_model → else last tiers entry → None
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ModelChoice {
    Pinned(String),
    Auto { bias: Option<Tier> },
}

pub fn parse_model_choice(raw: &str) -> ModelChoice;
// "auto" → Auto{None}; "auto:light|standard|heavy" → Auto{Some(_)};
// anything else (incl. "") → Pinned(raw.to_owned())

// Free fn over the builtin catalogue. tier is the *already-resolved* tier.
pub fn select_model(host: &str, choice: &ModelChoice, tier: Tier) -> Option<String>;
//   Pinned(s) if s.trim().nonempty → Some(s)         [pin always wins]
//   Pinned(empty/whitespace)       → None            [host default]
//   Auto{bias}                     → builtin().host(host)?
//                                       .model_for_tier(bias.unwrap_or(tier))
```

Two corrections to the plan's signatures:
- The plan writes `model_for_tier(&self, host, Tier)`. `host` is redundant — it's a method on `HostModels`, which already *is* the host entry. Drop the `host` param (signature above). The free-fn `select_model` does the `builtin().host(host)` lookup once.
- The plan's `select_model(catalogue, host, choice, ticket_complexity)` is dropped in favour of the `tier`-taking free-fn above. The "default `Standard` when `None`" rule moves to the **caller's** `Complexity→Tier` mapping (item 2), where `None → Standard`. `Auto{bias}` ignores the passed tier (hard override) — preserved.

**`Auto` bias precedence** (must be explicit, matches locked decision 3): in `select_model`, `Auto{Some(bias)}` uses `bias` and ignores the per-ticket `tier`. So a dispatcher always passes the ticket's resolved tier, and `select_model` discards it when a bias is present. Good.

**The "never returns `Some("auto")"` guarantee holds structurally:** `Auto` resolves only through `model_for_tier`, which only ever returns catalogue string literals or `None`; `"auto"` can only survive as `Pinned("auto")`, which the `models check` early-pass (item 6) and config default (`auto`) prevent from reaching a dispatcher as a pin. Keep the defended test.
